patch_description: The current program's Kalman + RTS backward smoother achieved the best score (0.67) by minimizing lag, slope changes, and false reversals. The crossover combines it with the strongest element from the inspiration scripts: the zero-phase bidirectional one-pole smoothing pass (from the first prior program), which cancels its own group delay while damping residual high-frequency ripple. Applied after the RTS smoother, this further reduces slope changes and false reversals with no added lag. The adaptive alpha is chosen from the residual noise level of the smoother output (MAD of first differences), so clean signals pass nearly untouched while noisy outputs get extra ripple suppression. The MAD-based noise estimate and adaptive process-noise machinery from the current program are retained unchanged, as is the exact output contract (y[i] ↔ input time i + window_size − 1). The bidirectional pass is vectorized-free but O(n), keeping efficiency_score at 1.0.
